Amanda C: Quick question — after the canary yesterday we started seeing OTLP exporter backlog spikes for a subset of prod routes. It coincides with enabling aggressive head sampling for the enterprise tier. Any quick wins to avoid tailing the exporters and blowing retention?
Jorge R: ugh yeah saw that. Head sampling at 100% for 3 routes + large request fanout = huge span volume. :grimacing:
Liam P: short term: drop head sample to something like 10-20% for the heavy routes and increase deterministic tail sampling for errors. That keeps most success traces thin.
Amanda C: does that mean changing sampling in the app or in the collector? We have customers on private deploys too — want consistent behavior.
Sree N: prefer collector-side rules so private/hosted consistent. Add a per-route attribute-based sampler in otel-collector and push lower head-sample for routes with high p95 size.
Oli M: +1. Also add exporter backpressure metrics to console so we can alarm before queues fill. Right now we only see dropped spans after the fact.
Jorge R: we hit this because exporter queue backs up and then the collector starts dropping - there was no graceful degradation. We should implement adaptive throttling: when exporter queue > 70% reduce sampling for non-error spans.
Amanda C: sounds good. Anyone have a config snippet we can iterate on?
Liam P: here's a minimal example for otel-collector using attributefilter + probabilistic sampler + a small script to flip rates via k8s configmap:```receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  tail_sampler:
    # sample all traces with error or high latency
    decision_wait: 1s
    num_traces: 100000
  probabilistic:
    sampling_percentage: 20
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tail_sampler, probabilistic]
      exporters: [otlp/jaeger]
```
Sree N: note: tail_sampler here is for tail sampling, but if exporter queue backs up we should programmatically lower `probabilistic.sampling_percentage` (or flip to 5%) via the control plane. ops-bot could watch queue metrics and update config.
ops-bot: alert: exporter_queue_utilization for exporter 'otlp/jaeger' at 78% on prod (detected by infra metrics).
Oli M: perfect — make ops-bot also trigger a canary config that reduces head sampling on top 5 noisy routes for 10 minutes, then revert.
Amanda C: is there any risk of losing signal for regression evals if we drop head sampling temporarily? We run prompt-based evals tied to spans for quality checks.
Jorge R: risk exists. Mitigation: tag spans used for eval with an attribute (e.g., `x-eval=true`) and whitelist them from sampling changes. Collector rules should honor that attribute first.
Liam P: +1. Also export a lightweight summary (count, lat buckets, error flag) at high frequency for heavy routes so we still have telemetry even when we sample traces heavily. That helps SLIs without requiring full spans.
Sree N: long term we should implement adaptive sampling that reacts to both exporter queue and SLO signals: target a fixed telemetry budget per tenant/route. If route exceeds budget, favor tail/errors + summary metrics.
Oli M: agree — and surface per-tenant budget burn rate in the console (per-route cost + predicted retention impact). UX ask for product: a simple slider to set telemetry budget per tenant with recommended defaults.
Amanda C: actionable list from this thread for infra sprint: 1) add exporter_queue_utilization alarms and ops-bot automation (Oli/Jorge) 2) implement collector-side per-route attribute sampler and control-plane toggles (Liam/Sree) 3) whitelist eval spans by attribute (Amanda/Jorge) 4) add lightweight route summaries export (Liam) 5) console telemetry budget UI spec (Oli/Product). I'll create tickets.
Jorge R: I'll start a PR with the adaptive throttle prototype and a small controller that watches queue metric and patches sampler config.
Liam P: I'll draft the collector config and the summary-exporter skeleton.
Oli M: I'll mock a console panel and wire the ops-bot automation.
Amanda C: thanks team. Let's try to have a small mitigation (ops-bot reduce head sample) out today as a stopgap.
Infra Bot: deploy started: sampling-throttle-controller v0.1 -> staging (triggered by Jorge R).
Amanda C: ping me when staging is green and we'll promote. :thumbsup:
